conviction_note: Hulic has raised its full-year forecast and dividend at the Q3 print in 2018, 2019, 2020, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. IFIS consensus for ordinary profit (188.3bn) already sits 1.8% above the plan, so the market expects the revision. My only edge is that the last two revisions (+4.2% and +3.6% on ordinary) were about twice what consensus implies. Against that, H1 progress is weaker than last year, margin longs outnumber margin shorts 6.45 to 1, and the stock fell on day two after last year's revision. Net, p_up is 54 on a 3.0 scale (+0.24 scaled), and the findings sum to +0.30.

Source: https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/report?bcode=3003 (IFIS/kabuyoho, read 2026-10-28 09:55 JST). The company plan is in the Q2 短信: https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260728/140120260727500129.pdf. This is one estimate source plus the company guide, so the bar is sourced, but only to one estimate.
positioning_check: JPX disclosed short register: 0.51% of shares, one seller, up 0.02pts from 0.49% (as of 2026-10-27, https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html, per the sealed baseline), so there is no crowded short and nothing to squeeze. 信用倍率 is 6.45 (broker scrape, per the baseline): leveraged retail is crowded long. Run-up is +4.25% over 20 sessions and +1.77% over 5, and the stock is about +7.9% off its 2026-10-08 low of 1,649. The baseline's priced lean is -0.35. There are no options, so no skew.

findings.finding: Hulic raises its full-year forecast and dividend at the Q3 print almost every year (2018, 2019, 2020, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, all at 11:30 on the Q3 day). The last two raised ordinary profit by +4.2% (2024) and +3.6% (2025) and the dividend by 2 and 3 yen. IFIS consensus of 188.3bn implies only about +1.8% on the 185bn plan, so a typical Hulic revision to about 191-192bn would clear the street. A 2-3 yen dividend raise fits the plan to lift the payout ratio from 40% to 45% by 2029.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 ritual revision days, measured from the prior close to the day-after close: 2023-10-27 +0.8% (1321 to 1332), 2024-10-28 +3.6% (1362.5 to 1412), 2025-10-28 -1.3% (1580.5 to 1560.5; +1.4% on the day, then -2.65% the next session). Mean about +1.0%, mixed sign. The market expects the revision; only its size against consensus moves the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: The revision itself is priced: consensus already sits above the plan, so a forecast simply held would be a mild negative. What may not be fully priced is the size. Consensus at +1.8% is about half of Hulic's last two revisions. If the market priced a typical Hulic raise, IFIS would read about 191-192bn, not 188.3bn. The counterweight sits in this finding's size, not in a separate number: H1 OP progress was 38.2% of plan against 42.2% at the same point last year, which argues for a smaller raise this year.
findings.independence: The revision record comes from irbank's disclosure list (https://irbank.net/3003/ir) and the 2024 notice (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20241028/140120241025502786.pdf). Both are the company's own history, so this is one line of evidence. The consensus comes from a different source (IFIS).

findings.finding: H1 operating profit carried a 5,129m yen special goodwill amortisation tied to Riso Kyoiku's share price. Riso closed higher at 2026-09-30 (208) than at 2026-06-30 (200), so Q3 should carry no similar extra charge, and the TOB at 295 announced 2026-10-13 lifts the price further for Q4. Underlying OP progress excluding the charge was 85.4bn, or 40.7% of the 210bn plan.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separate reaction on record. The H1 print that disclosed the charge rose +3.9% over two days (1835 to 1907 by 2026-07-29), so the charge did not weigh on that print.
findings.why_not_priced: The quarter-to-quarter dynamic of a price-linked goodwill charge on a subsidiary is a detail that consensus models likely smooth. But it is inside the company's guide and small against 210bn of OP, so it is close to zero.
findings.independence: Riso prices from https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/4714.T?range=1y&interval=1d; TOB terms from https://kabutan.jp/disclosures/pdf/20261013/140120261013549957/

findings.finding: Positioning is long into the print. 信用倍率 is 6.45 (crowded margin long), the stock is up about 7.9% in 14 sessions from the 2026-10-08 low of 1,649, and last year's Q3 revision gained on the day and was sold the next session (-2.65%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-28: +1.42% on the release day, then -2.65% the next session. 2026-07-28/29: +5.42% on the day after, then -4.06% and -3.88%. The name tends to give back gains after prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the baseline's lean of -0.35 already carries the margin overhang and the run-up. It is kept at a small size only because the day-two give-back has repeated on this name.
findings.independence: The margin ratio and short register are from the sealed baseline (JPX register, broker scrape), and the tape is from Yahoo. Both are positioning data, not company information.

outside_window.finding: The 180-day-type lock-up on the May 2026 overseas secondary offering (17.39m shares sold by Oki Electric, Yasuda Warehouse, Aomori Michinoku Bank and Katakura, as part of cross-shareholding unwinds) expires around late November 2026, after the window. The lock-up length is not confirmed in the document text I read.
Riso Kyoiku TOB at 295 yen (full ownership, about 84m shares, roughly 25bn yen) runs to 2026-11-26.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: expected, given the Q3 raise most years since 2018 and IFIS 1.8% above plan; the question is size against 188.3bn. Returns: a 2-3 yen dividend raise is likely with any net-profit raise (payout path 40% to 45%); no buyback expected. New-year guide: not at Q3. Quarter vs own 進捗率: H1 ordinary profit progress was 38.3% against 39.1% last year, and IFIS's Q3 cumulative bar of 106.6bn (57.6%) is above last year's 53.9%.
baseline_tension: The strongest positive the release could carry is a forecast and dividend raise larger than consensus, and I looked for it: it is the main finding, and it cuts mildly against the baseline's -0.35 lean and the crowded margin long. The run-up and margin ratio cut the other way, so the net is a small positive lean, not a call.
lessons_applied: Open question 4 (a five-day run-in sized as a short signal was wrong once) and the rule that agreeing with the priced lean is not a finding: positioning finding trimmed from -0.3 to -0.2.
